title: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality
title_zh: AI评估者偏爱由某些AI模型撰写的求职申请，而与候选人质量无关

paragraphs.en: 审计发现AI招聘评估者对特定写作模型存在系统性偏好与自偏好，导致合格候选人因模型不匹配被淘汰。 Job applicants increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to write cover letters, while employers deploy LLMs to screen them. In this all-AI setting, we ask whether the \emph{choice of model} affects hiring outcomes independently of candidate qualifications. We introduce a multi-model auditing framework pairing eleven LLM writer agents with nine API-hosted evaluator agents across ten job descriptions and fifty candidates per job. Four findings emerge. First, we identify a generative preference hierarchy: a consistent global ranking of writer models by evaluator acceptance, in which locally hosted models are systematically disadvantaged regardless of their license, compounded by self-preference bias where evaluators favour their own outputs. Second, evaluator models differ substantially in how much bias they introduce based on applicants' tool choice, offering actionable guidance for fairer screening design. Third, this hierarchy has measurable competitive consequences: in the most adverse pairing, approximately two (1.8) out of twenty-five qualified candidates are filtered out purely due to model mismatch. Fourth, a common mechanism explains the patterns above: writer preference and self-preference trace to a combination of how much each writer leans on specific stylistic cues and how strongly evaluators, often unanimously, reward or penalise those same cues. A further check finds little evidence that an unmeasured "writer fingerprint" remains once these same features are accounted for. We discuss implications for algorithmic fairness in employment, regulation of AI-assisted screening, and the design of auditing frameworks that can be reapplied as the model landscape evolves.
paragraphs.zh: 审计发现AI招聘评估者对特定写作模型存在系统性偏好与自偏好，导致合格候选人因模型不匹配被淘汰。求职者越来越多地使用大语言模型（LLM）来撰写求职信，而雇主则部署LLM来筛选这些求职信。 在这种全AI的场景中，我们探究模型的选择是否会在独立于候选人资质的情况下影响招聘结果。 我们提出一个多模型审计框架，将十一个LLM写作智能体与九个API托管的评估智能体配对，覆盖十份职位描述和每份职位五十名候选人。研究得出四项发现。 第一，我们识别出一个生成式偏好层级：评估者对写作模型接受度的一致全局排序，其中本地托管模型无论采用何种许可证均处于系统性劣势，且评估者偏爱自己输出的自偏好偏差进一步加剧了这一问题。 第二，不同评估者模型因申请人工具选择而引入偏差的程度差异显著，这为设计更公平的筛选机制提供了可操作的指导。 第三，这一层级具有可衡量的竞争后果：在最不利的配对中，二十五名合格候选人中约有两人（1.8人）纯粹因模型不匹配而被淘汰。 第四，一个共同的机制解释了上述模式：写作偏好和自偏好源于两方面因素的组合，即每个写作者对特定风格线索的依赖程度，以及评估者——通常是全体一致地——对这些相同线索的奖励或惩罚强度。 进一步的检查发现，一旦这些特征被纳入考量，几乎没有证据表明还存在未被测量的“写作者指纹”。 我们讨论了这些发现对就业领域算法公平性、AI辅助招聘筛选监管，以及可在模型格局演变时重复应用的审计框架设计的启示。
